partially_covered.missing: No explicit modeling of all organization attributes beyond address and identifier; some organization info (e.g., contact, legal status) not captured.
No formal encoding of D96A/EN 16931-1 mandatory fields or validation constraints (e.g., required identifiers, logical consistency).

cq_coverage.details: Nearly all CQs are answerable with the current classes and properties. CQ5 and CQ13 are partially covered due to missing detailed organization attributes and lack of explicit mandatory field constraints.

strengths: Well-structured class hierarchy with clear separation of concerns
Good use of OWL restrictions for required sections and assignments
Comprehensive use of property characteristics and disjointness
weaknesses: No use of General Class Axioms (GCAs)
No equivalence axioms for complex class definitions
Limited modeling of organization and item attributes beyond minimal fields

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing domain or range in some object properties (none detected, but double-check if ontology is extended)
P7: Lack of equivalence axioms for complex classes

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model additional organization attributes (e.g., contact info, legal entity type, VAT ID) and item details (e.g., classification, unit of measure) to fully answer CQ5 and similar queries.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves completeness for organization- and item-related questions.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Define explicit SHACL or OWL cardinality constraints for mandatory fields required by EN 16931-1 and D96A (e.g., invoice number, dates, identifiers).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables automated validation and full CQ13 coverage.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce General Class Axioms (GCAs) and/or owl:equivalentClass for core constructs such as InvoiceMessage or OrganizationRoleAssignment.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables richer reasoning and more robust ontology structure.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add further disjointness axioms between more sibling classes and consider using disjoint unions for sections.

summary: The ontology demonstrates strong structural modeling of UN/EDIFACT invoices, organizations, roles, and line items, with nearly complete CQ coverage and strict OWL 2 compliance. Some minor gaps remain in detailed organization attributes and formalization of mandatory field constraints. Quality is high, but could be further improved with GCAs, equivalence axioms, and richer attribute modeling.
